answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can use continuous path attestation: each agent must wander a unique 800-step trajectory across a public tundra lattice refreshed every epoch by external entropy. A distributed raven committee samples and re-computes three random segments; matches fail the agent. Generating 200 distinct non-overlapping paths costs an attacker roughly 160k steps plus collision resolution overhead exceeding 10^9 hashes, while one honest agent needs only 800. The scheme fails if the lattice entropy is delayed.
